posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: It sounds like a holographic diffusion screen.

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **Dinesh:** It sounds like a holographic diffusion screen.

...but may involve additional features. Take a look at [http://products3.3m.com/catalog/us/en00 ... utput_html](http://products3.3m.com/catalog/us/en001/electronics_mfg/vikuiti/node_6WDTKHF26Cge/root_GST1T4S9TCgv/vroot_S6Q2FD9X0Jge/theme_us_vikuiti_3_0/command_AbcPageHandler/output_html)

There are also mirror like reflectors, providing >98% reflectance.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: Ok, it doesn't sound holographic. It sounds like they've altered the polarisation of the input beam so that the front (or back, depending on which way the input face is called) polariser on the LCD sees all the input light at the same polarisation. The reflectivity curve looks a lot like standard reflectivity for p.
